newsitem.title: USA: Prudential restitution requests pour in - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Prudential restitution requests pour in - WSJ.

text.p: More than 700,000 policyholders of Prudential Insurance Co of America have indicated they plan to seek restitution as part of a settlement concerning alleged deceptive sales practices, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Friday's electronic edition, the Journal said that restitution for that many policyholders could cost the company more than $1.6 billion.
That amount is more than Prudential had expected, but less than had been projected by some state insurance regulators and critics of the company, the Journal said.
Policyholders have until Sunday to indicate they plan to seek restitution.
A federal judge in March had approved an offer by Prudential to pay at least $410 million to policyholders to settle the class-action dispute over its sales practices.
Under the settlement, people who purchased as many as 10.7 million permanent life insurance policies between 1982 and 1995 are eligible for restitution.
The lawsuit had claimed that Prudential agents misled thousands of policyholders into buying more-expensive life insurance they already had with the company.

Insurance analysts said it is too early to determine the ultimate financial price of the settlement since it is not yet known how many policyholders will actually follow through with claims nor how much each of them will receive.
A Prudential spokesman said the company would not release any participation figures until the restitution program ends, which could be months from now.
